source.title: Why do small language models underperform? Studying Language Model Saturation via the Softmax Bottleneck
source.authors: Nathan Godey; Éric Villemonte de la Clergerie; Benoît Sagot

record.tranche_reason: The paper measures Pythia pretraining loss and compares smaller-model checkpoints with a fitted scaling curve; it reports late-training loss increases and departures from the curve, qualifying the scaling-law claim.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the Pythia pretraining-loss trajectories and their comparison with the fitted curve. The downstream benchmark table is recorded as related evidence, but it does not test downstream predictability. Anisotropy, singular-value, rank-constrained-head, and 5-gram results are not rows because they do not measure the scaling-law outcomes in the claim versions.
record.test_reason: The study measures Pythia in-domain Pile loss across sizes and checkpoints. It fits a Hoffmann-style L(N,T) on models of 410M and up and reports that smaller models fall short of it and that their loss rises late in training. That is a result showing where a single power law bends or fails. It is not a reproduction of the original sweeps.
record.authors_conclusion: Broadly correct. The authors conclude that small LMs saturate in late training: loss rises and they underperform scaling-law extrapolation by about 8%. They attribute this to the softmax bottleneck, where a linear head on hidden dimension under about 1000 cannot match the high-rank contextual distribution. The saturation co-occurs with last-layer anisotropy and spectral collapse of the head.
record.recipe_differences: Uses released Pythia checkpoints and an in-domain cross-entropy measurement, then fits a Hoffmann-style scaling relation on larger models and compares smaller checkpoints with it; it is not a reproduction of the original large-scale scaling experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported outcome varies with checkpoint selection: final checkpoints underperform the fitted curve more than best checkpoints. The paper attributes the best-checkpoint shortfall partly to incomplete learning-rate cooldown.

fits_no_version.finding: With frozen bodies, constraining LM-head rank below about 1000 noticeably raises loss, regardless of model size (Fig. 6). The authors tie small-model saturation to hidden dimension under 1000 (softmax bottleneck).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: A low hidden or head dimension (under about 1000) bottlenecks LM loss independently of parameter count, a candidate mechanism for small models deviating from scaling laws.

fits_no_version.finding: Pythia-160M best checkpoints beat final checkpoints on six zero-shot metrics.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Downstream scores degrade alongside late-training loss saturation in small models.

record.problems: The authors note that only a relatively small number of saturated models could be studied and that the extensive intermediate checkpoints are available only for Pythia in the relevant size range. The loss-curve and anisotropy comparisons are shown in figures without reported uncertainty estimates; the scaling-curve departures are reported as aggregates rather than per-model values.
record.rows_left_out: No relevant loss or downstream-evaluation results were left out. Other reported measurements (anisotropy, singular-value distributions, rank-constrained heads, and n-gram matrix rank) do not directly measure the scaling-law claim versions.

untested.parts: Token and compute scaling where the other quantities are not bottlenecks. The quality of the power-law fit over the 410M+ models is not reported.
All. The fit is on larger models and is compared with smaller ones, not small-to-large prediction.
All. There is no fixed-compute allocation analysis.
All. Width/depth trade-offs at fixed N are discussed but not run. The rank-constrained head experiment is not a shape comparison at fixed parameter count.
All. Downstream scores are reported only for best vs final checkpoints of Pythia-160M.

missing.what: Loss trajectories on the Wikipedia test set for Pythia 14M–410M, showing saturation from which the models 'never seem to fully recover'.
Per-model deviations from the fitted curve and the goodness of fit on the 410M+ models. Only figure-level data and averages are given.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'challenges' label on V1 is downgraded. The late loss rise occurs in a parameter-bottlenecked regime that V1 excludes. The cross-size shortfall shows a scope limit below 410M, not an absence of the power law. The fit reuses Chinchilla's B, β and E and fits only A and α, a fit-dependence worth noting. Preprint.

versions.untested_parts: No independent token-count or compute sweep with the other quantities non-bottlenecking; evidence is limited to Pythia loss across model sizes and training checkpoints, using an in-domain Pile sample.
The paper fits on larger models and compares smaller models with the fit; it does not fit on small runs and predict runs orders of magnitude larger.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token scaling.
No controlled comparison of depth, width, or other architecture choices at fixed parameter count.
No other modality, repeated-data, fine-tuning, or transfer scaling-law test.
The paper reports best-versus-final downstream scores for one checkpointed model, but does not test whether downstream performance is predictable from scale or pretraining loss.
The paper reports smaller-model departures from a fitted curve, but does not systematically vary parameter counting, training schedule, data, or fitting method, or compare published exponents.

rows.subject: Pythia models below 410M parameters (aggregate)

rows.operation_detail: Compared final-checkpoint loss with a scaling curve fitted on models ranging from 410M parameters upward.

conditions.value: 50k tokens randomly sampled from The Pile
Hoffmann-style relation; fit A and α on larger models, reuse B = 410.7, β = 0.28, E = 1.69

rows.measure: Cross-entropy loss relative to fitted-curve prediction
rows.value: final checkpoints underperform the extrapolation by 8% in average
rows.note: The fit gives A = 119.09 and α = 0.246. The reported aggregate is an average; per-model deviations are not stated.
rows.check: The state is relative to V1: the power law in N fitted on 410M+ models overpredicts small-model performance by 8% on average, so it does not extend below 410M. For V7 this is an observed departure from a single curve. Only A and α were fitted, with B, β and E reused from Hoffmann. Per-model deviations and fit quality are not reported.

relationships.condition: Pythia models below 410M (hidden dim under 1000), compared with a Hoffmann-style fit on models of 410M and up
relationships.reason: Small models underperform the power-law extrapolation by 8% on average (final) and about 4% (best), so the N power law does not hold below this size here (R6, R7).
relationships.display_finding: Final and best checkpoints underperformed the power-law extrapolation by an average 8% and approximately 4%, respectively.
